after: ## What the brief says about Criterion C
alt: Criteria A, B and D are assessed in the on-screen examination; criterion C, speaking, is a separate interactive examination worth 24 marks that responds to multimodal texts. The classroom teacher marks it against the MYP year 5 criteria, the IB moderates a sample from each school and grades are adjusted where needed.
caption: Speaking is a separate, teacher-marked, IB-moderated conversation worth 24 marks.

alt: Four steps applied to a Repair Café poster: see (a teenager and an older man fixing a bike wheel, smiling), read (the headline “Don’t bin it – fix it!” and the icons), think (repair rather than throw away; two generations learning from each other) and relate (things thrown away locally, with a counter-view). Steps 1 and 2 are safe ground; 3 and 4 show range and thinking.
caption: Describe, read, interpret, then relate it to your world with a view.

after: ### Worked example: extending a flat answer
alt: Asked whether they would volunteer at a Repair Café, a flat answer is “Yes, I would.” The extended answer adds a reason, a past example (fixing a grandmother’s radio) and a conditional consequence (practising more and teaching younger children), using present, past and conditional forms.
caption: Answer, reason, example, consequence: one line becomes four.

alt: Six interaction strategies with English models: ask for repetition, check meaning, paraphrase a missing word, give a view and invite one, self-correct, and hold the turn. For an unexpected question: buy time, narrow it to something you can answer, and link back to vocabulary from the stimulus.
caption: Never switch to a memorised paragraph that does not answer the question.

alt: Three bars of 4, 3 and 2 minutes for the same stimulus, nine minutes in all, so the same ideas come out more smoothly each round. Tips: learn chunks, pause at phrase boundaries and use target-language fillers. For accuracy, open with a safe structure, then stretch to one more complex form.
caption: Say the same ideas in less time to make them flow.

alt: A six-step weekly cycle for the last term: collect stimuli linked to the global contexts, a two-minute read listing words for the image and text, speak with a partner who asks follow-ups, record and review, do the 4-3-2 drill, and refresh the phrase bank in the target language.
caption: Train spontaneous speaking every week, not recitation.
